recipes.name: Tres Leches Piña Colada Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (18.25 ounce) box yellow cake mix without pudding
1 tablespoon toasted flaked coconut, or as desired

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Stir together yellow cake mix, water, eggs, and vegetable oil in a large bowl until moistened; beat with an electric mixer on medium speed for 2 minutes. Stir in crushed pineapple until incorporated. Pour batter into the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is lightly browned and a toothpick inserted into the center of cake comes out clean or with moist crumbs, 30 to 40 minutes. Remove cake from the oven.
Whisk together cream of coconut and milk in a medium bowl until smooth; pour mixture over hot cake. Allow cake to cool thoroughly.
Whip together heavy cream and sugar in a separate bowl using an electric mixer until soft peaks form. Frost the top of cake with whipped cream and sprinkle with toasted coconut.

raw_recipe.headline: Tres Leches Piña Colada Cake
raw_recipe.description: An easy version of the beloved tres leches cake is made with cake mix, pineapple, and cream of coconut to give the cake a piña colada flavor.

video.description: Indulge in a decadent showstopper of a dessert! In this sweet and surprisingly light treat, yellow sponge cake is soaked in cream, milk and in a tropical twist, cream of coconut. Crushed pineapple and toasted coconut add pina colada flavor and eggs add an extra richness. With a smooth topping of whipped cream, this cake is very easy to sink your fork into and even easier to make disappear!

review.reviewBody: Ok so I reviewed this a few months ago and I said I added some sweetened condensed milk to sweeten up the milk & coconut cream bcuz the coco cream was not sweet at all. Today I made the cake again and this time decided to use Goya brand coconut cream and it's sweet! So there's sweet coconut cream and unsweetened coconut cream...never knew that until today! Hope this helps!
Everyone that tried it, loved it. Next time, we are going to add some rum to it. Loved the whipped topping, made it a lighter-tasting cake.

Amazing! I thought this might be too soggy once I pored the coconut cream on but it wasn't. Also, instead of regular milk, I used coconut milk. I also whipped 2.5 cups of heavy cream with 1/2 cup sugar and it turned out to be a perfect ratio. RAVE REVIEWS a!!

Cake mixes are not as large now. The one I bought, Duncan Heinz,the only one I could find without pudding, was 16.5 ounces, so we added 1.7 ounces of flour. I was worried about whether or not the pineapple should have been drained or not. I didn't drain it. I used more toasted coconut on top, probably about a cup. We also added a little rum to the whipping cream. The cake was a HUGE hit at the dinner party to which we took it. We'll probably cut down on the milk next time. YUM!!
My family loved it. I added coconut to the batter, used apple sauce instead of oil, and cut down the water to 1 cup. Also used light cool whip instead of whipping the cream myself.

Everyone that tried this cake, LOVED it (even people who claim to NOT like cake)! It is not too sweet and not too wet for my liking...just perfect. But, as other reviewers have done, I also used about 1/4 of a cup of toasted coconut on top. Thanks for a great recipe!

Delicious! I made a mistake and just poured the cream of coconut over the cake and didn’t add the milk. It was still yummy. It was even better the next day after the liquid fully absorbed. It was really delicate next day right out of the refrigerator. I added more roasted coconut to the top (about a cup) because my family loves coconut. Easy and so good!

The BEST cake I've ever made! I made this for a senior lunch today and there wasn't even crumbs left! I'm not much of a cake lover but I could have eaten half of this! It was so easy to make! I followed directions except to substitute Cool Whip for the whipped cream frosting. Made it yesterday, used a skewer to poke holes in it after I took it out of the oven, poured the cream of coconut and milk (2% because it's all I had) mixture over it. Moved it to the refrigerator after it cooled then covered it with Cool Whip and topped with toasted coconut this morning. Got rave reviews!

I had unsweetened coconut milk so I replaced the regular milk with a can of condensed milk! I also poked some holes in the cake with a skewer! The crowd went wild! DELICIOUS! FYI! Always read comments because I would have not known about sweetened & unsweetened coconut milk!

We made this for a group at our son's 24th Birthday Dinner. Everyone raved about the dessert. Our family has Latin heritage - so we like Tres Leches cake. But this is much better. It is less sweet, and just as moist! The pineapple gives is an extra special flavor. I find it so much more interesting and special than a regular Tres Leches, or a regular Birthday Cake. I searched desserts extensively on this website for something special for this dinner, and I am so glad I came across this one. I made it prettier by making a raspberry puree sauce to write the birthday greeting with his name on top of the cake, with a decoration. This cake is a winner!

This was a BIG hit with our friends, all of whom had eaten traditional tres leches cake previously, including one who ate it more than once in Costa Rica. I drained the pineapple and substituted the juice for part of the water called for in the cake batter. The only other change was making a larger quantity of toasted coconut and serving it on the side, since not everyone appreciates coconut, and those who did could enjoy it to their personal taste. I will definitely make it again and will probably make it the same way.
Love the final product great taste

I’ve been making this cake since the 1990s. Only thing I do different is instead of milk, I use sweetened condensed milk and frost with Cool Whip, but real whipped cream is amazing too. People always ask me to make this cake for every occasion. It’s that good. I’ve done it with and without coconut on top, good either way.
Used evaporated milk instead of cream of coconut. Maybe 1/4 c liquid not absorbed. Thanks for recipe. Served at Mexican luncheon and all enjoyed.
This is the second time I've made this cake and I substituted the water for apple juice. It jacked up the pina colada taste considerably. I also used a spring form pan to fancy it up a bit.
Everyone loves it everytime I make it... sometimes like today I didnt put pinapples.. its still SUPER DELIOUS
what wonderful cake, i made it for a party was a big hit.

This cake is awesome! I’ve made it twice. I wanted it a little sweeter so I put a splash of vanilla in my batter and a splash of rum in the topping. People are already asking me to bring it to get togethers.
Thanks for a great recipe
Everyone loved it!! I added some pineapple juice to the milk mixture.
